not_found: van Duijn, Witte, Zinkstok, Hogervorst, Eur. Phys. J. D 19, 25 (2002): isotope shifts and 105Pd hyperfine constants of the 276.4, 247.7 and 244.9 nm ground-state lines (and the J=1 upper levels 40368.796, 40838.874 cm-1). Paper is paywalled; only abstract + 2-page preview opened. Only second-hand numbers are given here (3P°1 A, B via Geldhof 2020; linewidth lifetimes via Xu 2006).

Channappa & Pendlebury 1965: 105Pd hyperfine constants and g_J of 4d9 5s 3D1 (10093.992) and 1D2 (11721.809), and measured g_J of all four 4d9 5s levels: abstract only (no numbers). Kümmel, Baumann, Kischkel 1993 (3D1, 1D2 hyperfine structure): abstract only.
Lifetimes of the metastable 4d9 5s levels: no measurement located.

Precise (frequency-comb or wavemeter-calibrated absolute) transition frequencies of Pd I: none located; best wavenumbers remain the FTS level energies of Engleman, Litzén, Lundberg, Wyart, Phys. Scr. 57, 345 (1998) already in NIST ASD.
Doidge, Spectrochim. Acta B 50, 209 (1995): compilation of resonance-line oscillator strengths, not opened; its three Pd log gf values are quoted second-hand in the conflicts list.

Experimental branching fractions for the 34068.977, 35451.443, 36975.973, 38811.896, 39858.361 cm-1 levels: none; only HFR theory (Xu et al. 2006 Table 3) is given for those 17 lines and flagged as theory.
A demonstrated laser-cooling experiment on Pd: none located; the 340.5 nm 3D3 -> 3F°4 line is the closed cycling candidate.
conflicts: Lifetimes of 4d9 5p J=1 levels from natural linewidths (van Duijn et al. 2002: 5.2(3), 3.1(2), 4.3(2) ns for 36180.677, 40368.796, 40838.874 cm-1) are systematically shorter than the time-resolved LIF values (Xu et al. 2006: 7.6(3), 5.0(2), 4.8(2) ns), Biémont et al. 1982 and the Hanle values; Xu et al. attribute this to residual broadening in the linewidth analysis. LIF values kept as entries.
36180.677 cm-1 lifetime: Budick 1968 Hanle value 8.7(9) ns is higher than 7.6(3) (Xu), 7.7(4) (Biémont), 7.46(32) (Baumann & Liening).
34068.977 cm-1 lifetime: Hanle 6.90(76) ns (Baumann & Liening 1971) vs LIF 8.9(4) ns (Biémont et al. 1982).

Resonance-line transition probabilities: Xu et al. 2006 (measured lifetime x measured branching fraction) give A = 1.03(10)e7, 5.3(9)e7, 6.2(11)e7 s^-1 for 276.4, 247.7, 244.9 nm, whereas the NIST lines file (tp_ref T7227 = Morton, ApJS 130, 403 (2000) compilation) has 1.69e7, 1.18e7, 1.11e7 s^-1. Xu et al. list the Doidge 1995 compilation log gf = -1.237, -1.284, -1.523 against their -1.45, -0.83, -0.78. The 247.7 and 244.9 nm values differ by a factor of about 5.

105Pd hyperfine constants of 4d9 5p 2[7/2]°4 (35927.948 cm-1): Sulai & Mueller 2020 A = -79.7(3), B = -469.9(1.8) MHz vs Liening 1974 A = -87(2), B = -330(30) MHz (significant disagreement, noted by Sulai & Mueller).

105Pd 4d9 5s 3D3 A constant from Channappa & Pendlebury 1965 is quoted as -391.179(1) MHz by Sulai & Mueller and -391.178(1) MHz by Geldhof et al. (original not opened). Sulai & Mueller attribute the values -391.5(4) / -650(5) MHz to Liening 1974, but these are exactly the "This work" values of Geldhof et al. 2020; treated here as Geldhof 2020.
105Pd 4d9 5s 3D2 (7755.025 cm-1): Geldhof 2020 A = 64.2(4) MHz vs Channappa & Pendlebury 66.359(1) MHz (5 sigma of the statistical-only laser error).

363.6 nm isotope shifts: Geldhof 2022 reanalysis differs from Geldhof 2020 by up to 6 MHz (within the quoted systematic error); converted to the same reference, Sulai & Mueller give 104-108 = 964.3(2.1) MHz (derived) vs 958.1(6)[13.0] MHz.
Xu et al. 2006 Table 2 prints 325.16361 nm for the 40771.510 -> 10093.992 line (typo; correct air wavelength 325.87765 nm), and their Table 3 column headed A_ki actually lists g_k A_ki.
notes: Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second). Sulai & Mueller tabulate nu(A) - nu(106); Geldhof et al. tabulate delta nu(108,A) = nu(A) - nu(108); both kept as printed, so keys use 106 or 108 as the second isotope. For the Geldhof values "unc" is the statistical and "unc_syst" the systematic (acceleration/cooler voltage) uncertainty; the 105Pd values refer to the hyperfine centre of gravity. Level lifetimes: Xu et al. 2006 (time-resolved LIF, six levels) where available, otherwise Biémont et al. 1982 (time-resolved LIF on an atomic beam); other measurements and HFR theory under lifetime.alternatives. A_s for the 20 lines of Xu et al. Table 2 are experimental (A = BF/tau) and were converted from the printed g_k A_ki by dividing by 2J_upper+1; the 17 lines from their Table 3 are HFR theory (method "theory") and should only be used where nothing measured exists. NIST A values exist for only 8 Pd I lines (5 from Biémont et al. 1982, 3 from Morton 2000). Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: ionization_limit, lifetime.alternatives, hyperfine.<A>.alternatives, isotope_shift_other, linewidth_MHz, unc_syst, note. Hyperfine constants follow E = A K/2 + B [3K(K+1)/4 - I(I+1)J(J+1)] / [2I(2I-1)J(2J-1)]; 105Pd has I = 5/2 and negative magnetic moment (inverted structure for most levels). LS names in parentheses in the labels are those used by the cited papers (3D3, 3P2, 3F4, ...); NIST uses J1K notation.
